## On-Call Handoff — Gateway 503s

**Status:** Ongoing as of last log entry (03:59:27Z) — not yet resolved.

**Root cause:** `dep-4471` (gateway, deployed by a.novak, 02:12:00Z–02:14:00Z) — config change *"connection-per-request for pool isolation"*, which flipped `gateway.pool.perRequest: false -> true` (applied at 02:13:41.234Z, config generation 118→119). This appears to have multiplied concurrent connection demand against a fixed pool cap of 20, causing pool exhaustion within ~33 seconds of the config taking effect.

**Impact window:** 2026-03-14 **02:14:18.972Z** (first 503, `ERR_POOL_EXHAUSTED`) through at least **03:59:27.974Z** (end of available log), so **≥1h45m** and still active. Errors recur in ~60s bursts (4-5 consecutive 503s per burst, one burst per checkout cycle), hitting all backend services roughly evenly (billing-svc, orders-svc, catalog-svc, accounts-svc) — confirms it's gateway-side pool starvation, not a single downstream failure. Queue depth (`waiting`) climbed from 13 at onset to 74 by 03:59, so it's not self-healing. `/health` checks return 200 throughout — process is alive, just starved.

**Scope:** Gateway only. Checked `worker.log` for the same window — workers show no pool exhaustion, no 503s, and flat `db_wait` throughout; the job fleet was unaffected.

**Action: roll back `dep-4471`** (or hotfix `gateway.pool.perRequest` back to `false`) to relieve pool pressure. No other deploy in `deploys.csv` is implicated — `dep-4472` (billing-svc, 02:41) and `dep-4473` (catalog-svc, 03:20) both landed after the errors were already underway.
